newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary won't scrap energy plan - commissioner.
newsitem.headline: Hungary won't scrap energy plan - commissioner.

text.p: A commissioner appointed to review Hungary's stalled plans to hike energy rates to world market levels said on Tuesday the plan will be revised but not scrapped.
"From a professional view it will be the continuation of the work done so far," the commissioner, Imre Karl, told a news conference.
"There is manoeuvering area in what costs the government should recognise now," he added.

Hungary recently postponed an energy price rice previously announced for October 1, provoking irate reactions from foreign investors who last year purchased controlling stakes in Hungary's energy distribution companies and power stations.

The government said the January 1 date still meets a deadline stipulated in the energy law, by which time companies which bought stakes in formerly state-owned energy distributor companies are guaranteed an eight percent profit margin relative to the capital of the company.
Karl and the group of experts he recruited in the past few days will have to review the proposal for the rate of the price hikes as recommended by the Hungarian Energy Office (MEH).
Karl said his experts will not have to start the MEH's work again, only change certain points of the MEH's report.
"This is partly economic, partly political work, the two things have to be alloyed," he said.
The commissioner said he would examine the macroeconomic implications of price rises and their impact on inflation.
But he added the Socialist-led ruling coalition would have to consider the impact on ordinary Hungarians.
"Energy and energy privatisation is a shaky political matter everywhere," he said.
Real wages dropped some 10 percent in Hungary last year and are expected to decline by around further two percent this year.
"There are many people who cannot pay for the energy bill, or cannot buy proper clothing for themselves," Karl said.
